papers.title: Rapid mixing of Potts Glauber dynamics throughout uniqueness
papers.abstract: Sampling from the ferromagnetic $q$-state Potts model is a fundamental problem in statistical physics and approximate counting. Although computationally hard in the worst case, sampling is expected to be efficient throughout the high-temperature uniqueness regime of the model using the natural single-site Glauber dynamics. We establish fast mixing bounds for every $q$, in the full high-temperature regimes in the two central graph families on $n$ vertices. (1) For every $\Delta\ge 3$, the Potts Glauber dynamics mixes in $n\operatorname{polylog}(n)$ steps with high probability on a uniformly random $\Delta$-regular graph for all $\beta<\beta_u(q,\mathbb T_\Delta)$ where $\beta_u(q,\mathbb T_\Delta)$ is the uniqueness threshold on the $\Delta$-regular tree; (2) For every $d\ge 2$, the Potts Glauber dynamics has inverse spectral gap $n^{1+o(1)}$ on cubes or tori in $\mathbb Z^d$ for all $\beta<\beta_c(q,\mathbb Z^d)$ where $\beta_c(q,\mathbb Z^d)$ is the critical point on $\mathbb Z^d$. Both temperature thresholds are sharp as the Glauber dynamics slows down exponentially above them. These results overcome the challenge of bounding mixing times without access to correlation decay bounds in the presence of pinnings (i.e., without spectral independence or strong spatial mixing). For this purpose, our proof introduces a new dichotomy principle: throughout the high-temperature regime, any initial spin distribution is either such that its pinnings ensure good correlation decay, or Glauber dynamics escapes from that distribution quickly. We expect this kind of dichotomy to have further applications. As a demonstration, we also develop its analog for random-cluster dynamics and use it to prove that Swendsen-Wang dynamics on random $\Delta$-regular graphs mixes in $O(\log n)$ time throughout uniqueness. The results in this paper were arrived at with the assistance of ChatGPT 5.6 and 6.

papers.title: Site Percolation on Multi-dimensional Lattice
papers.abstract: Sites in an infinite d-dimensional lattice, open with probability greater or equal to 1/d, form an infinite open path.

papers.title: SKFitter: Symmetry resolved Slater Koster tight-binding models from first principles for s, p, d and f electrons, spin orbit coupling and magnetism
papers.abstract: Constructing accurate and physically interpretable tight binding (TB) Hamiltonians from first principles calculations remains challenging, particularly for materials exhibiting complex orbital hybridization, spin orbit coupling (SOC), and magnetic order. SKFitter is an open-source Python framework for constructing and optimizing symmetry resolved Slater Koster TB models directly from density functional theory (DFT) calculations performed using Quantum ESPRESSO or VASP. The framework supports s to f orbitals, incorporates on site SOC and site resolved magnetic exchange interactions, and accommodates both orthogonal and nonorthogonal basis. A central feature is the symmetry resolved parameterization of orbital manifolds, which allows independent two centre hopping integrals between symmetry allowed orbital groups and across distinct neighbour shells. SKFitter also identifies missing orbital contributions and guide systematic basis set refinement and optimizes parameters through weights. The resulting Hamiltonian can be used to evaluate anomalous (AHC) and spin Hall conductivities (SHC), and topological invariants. We demonstrate the framework using eight representative materials spanning semimetals, semiconductors, transition metals, f-electron compounds, and magnetic systems. Symmetry resolved models achieve band energy errors of 9 to 41 meV within 1 eV of the Fermi level. The fitted Hamiltonians reproduce characteristic features of the SHC response of Pt, the SOC dependence of the AHC of Fe, and the momentum dependent altermagnetic spin splitting of MnTe without any altermagnet specific interaction. For EuMn2Bi2, projection guided orbital refinement reduces the near Fermi level fitting error from 120 to 32 meV. Together, these results establish SKFitter as a flexible and reproducible framework for developing symmetry consistent, physically interpretable TB models of complex materials.

papers.title: Sample complexity of quantum resource testing via one-shot quantum blurring
papers.abstract: Quantum resource testing is a fundamental primitive of quantum information processing, profoundly connected to resource manipulation. Its goal is to discriminate $n$ copies of a given resourceful state $\rho$ from all free (i.e., resourceless) states; key instances for applications are entanglement testing and quantum magic testing. The asymptotic characterisation relies on the recently proven Generalised Quantum Stein's Lemma (GQSL), which establishes the rate of decay of the false negative error probability for a fixed false positive error probability. This result, however, is intrinsically asymptotic and thus can provide no finite-resource guarantees, which makes its practical implications unclear. Here, we establish the first rigorous finite-$n$ bounds on quantum resource testing and hence quantum resource manipulation, thus strengthening the GQSL and providing explicit estimates on the number of copies needed to achieve a prescribed performance. As notable consequences, we obtain (a) the convergence of the regularised R\'enyi relative entropies of a resource, which settles the important open problem from [Fang/Hayashi, arXiv:2508.12901, IEEE ToIT 72:6, 2026]; and (b) the first sample-complexity bound for asymmetric resource testing: for any fixed false positive error probability, a false negative error probability of at most $\delta$ can be achieved with $n=O\left(\frac{\log(1/\delta)}{D^\infty(\rho\|\mathcal F)}\right)$ copies of $\rho$, in the limit where $\delta \to 0$.

papers.title: Exponential stability of port-Hamiltonian systems with unstructured, measurable Hamiltonian densities
papers.abstract: For first-order port-Hamiltonian systems in the dissipative setting considered here, we characterise exponential stability without any further regularity or block-structure assumption on the Hamiltonian density, thus closing a gap persisting in the literature. The proof requires revisiting the computation of the adjoint generator of the port-Hamiltonian semigroup. Finally, we provide both examples and non-examples showcasing the inconclusiveness of known conditions on the Hamiltonian densities necessary for the application of characterisation results in the literature.

papers.title: Fractional Differential Equations in Chemical Modeling: From Memory and Anomalous Transport to Mathematically Justified Models
papers.abstract: Fractional differential equations are increasingly used to model memory and anomalous transport in chemistry and related fields. However, the formal replacement of an integer-order derivative by a fractional one does not by itself justify fractional dynamics. The essential issue is whether nonlocality can be derived from a physical, stochastic, geometric, or reduction mechanism and whether it leads to experimentally testable consequences. This review, written primarily for mathematicians and specialists in fractional analysis, discusses representative applications in electrochemistry, adsorption and sorption, reaction--subdiffusion, chemical and enzyme kinetics, polymer relaxation, and atmospheric chemistry. Particular attention is paid to distinguishing mechanism-based fractional models from phenomenological fractionalizations. Mathematical questions of well-posedness, nonnegativity, conservation laws, dimensional consistency, parameter identifiability, and numerical convergence are emphasized. Experimental electrochemical examples illustrate the need to distinguish genuine fractional effects from model mismatch or non-identifiability. Several open problems connecting fractional analysis with experimentally grounded chemical modeling are formulated.

papers.title: Baker--Akhiezer sections from Higgs bundles and Landau levels in hyperbolic band theory
papers.abstract: As observed by Kienzle and the second author, rank-two $\mathcal{O}(3)$-twisted Higgs bundles on the projective line encode all hyperbolic crystals of genus two: the spectral curves are the unit cells, and the Hitchin fibers are the abelian Brillouin zones. In a uniform magnetic field of two flux quanta, the lowest Landau level is one-dimensional at every nonzero momentum, and, as found by Iengo and Li, its dimension jumps to two at the zero momentum. We identify the states of the lowest Landau level with the Baker--Akhiezer sections of the Higgs bundles, and their zeros, the vortices, with the Baker--Akhiezer divisors. A family of nonzero momenta limits to the zero momentum exactly when each of the two vortices approaches the image of the other under the spatial inversion, and the states of the jumped level are labeled by the directions of limiting. On the Higgs bundle side, the zero momentum is the point where the Hitchin fiber intersects the Hitchin section. Such a family of Higgs bundles limits to the Hitchin section, thereby crossing to a lower stratum of the \BB stratification, an example of the phenomenon investigated in terms of Baker--Akhiezer divisors by the first author with Figiel and Teschner.

papers.title: A note on surjective endomorphisms of Smale spaces
papers.abstract: We give conditions that are all equivalent to surjectivity for endomorphisms of irreducible Smale spaces. This extends results previously obtained by Hedlund~\cite{hedlund-endomorphisms} for full shifts, by Coven and Paul and by Lind and Marcus for irreducible subshifts of finite type.

papers.title: A Model for Fast Mining Blockchains
papers.abstract: We study a Markovian model for a blockchain mining process. In the limit where there is an infinite number of miners, the model satisfies a functional law of large numbers due to Barbour and Luczac (2008), leading to an infinite set of coupled ODEs characterising the blockchain heights. We show that the sequence of solutions to this system converges uniformly, to a limiting profile in an appropriate comoving frame. Utilising asymptotic arguments inspired by Brunet and Derrida (1997), we derive an explicit expression for the position of the travelling front, which exhibits a leading order logarithmic Bramson correction in time. For a finite number of miners, we further derive a correction to the travelling speed which is logarithmic in the number of miners. Finally, by application of a computation due to Ablowitz and Zeppetella (1979), we identify that, for a specific choice of the travelling speed, the Painlev\'e integrable, travelling wave solution of the Fisher-KPP equation with drift accurately matches our limiting profile. Our results are supported by numerical simulations.

papers.title: Delocalized region of bipartite Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graphs
papers.abstract: We consider bipartite Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graphs $\mathbb{G}(n, p, d/\sqrt{np})$ with two parts of sizes $n$ and $p$, respectively, and edge probability $d/\sqrt{pn}$. We show that for $d > b_* \log (n+p)$ all eigenvectors of its adjacency matrix, with eigenvalues away from zero, are delocalized with high probability. The threshold $b_*$ is an explicit function of the size ratio $n/p$ and optimal for eigenvector delocalization near the spectral edges. Our results extend to bulk eigenvectors down to the optimal threshold $d\geq \mathcal{D}\sqrt{\log (n+p)}$ for a constant $\mathcal D \geq 1$. In the supercritical scale $d \gg \log (n+p)$ we show that all eigenvectors are delocalized. Our results also hold for sparse rectangular random matrices with independent entries.

papers.title: The Floquet-Magnus expansion of unbounded operators
papers.abstract: The Floquet-Magnus expansion is a widely used tool to derive effective descriptions of time-periodic quantum systems by approximating their dynamics with a time-independent Hamiltonian. However, its standard formulation is, strictly speaking, restricted to bounded Hamiltonians. In this work, we extend its definition and analysis to a broad class of time-periodic unbounded Hamiltonians. Our approach is based on an a priori distinct nonperturbative framework for the construction of effective Hamiltonians, which we show to reproduce the Floquet-Magnus expansion. A particular strength of our framework is that it allows us to prove that the resulting effective dynamics approximates the original time evolution propagators to arbitrary order in the high-frequency limit without requiring convergence of the Floquet-Magnus expansion, a condition that is already highly restrictive even in the bounded setting. We illustrate the scope of the method on representative models: the quantum Rabi Hamiltonian in the interaction picture, and the periodically driven quantum harmonic oscillator.

papers.title: The $\varepsilon$-smoothed Entanglement of Formation and its relation to the Moreau-Yosida approximation
papers.abstract: We describe a family of convex continuous functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, on the set of states of a bipartite quantum system (consisting of finite-dimensional or infinite-dimensional subsystems) obtained by applying the Mora-Piani-Briegel construction of $\varepsilon$-measure (proposed in [Phys. Rev. A 109, 052413]) to the Entanglement of Formation (EoF) with the use of the trace norm distance in the role of basic metric. These functions are non-increasing in $\varepsilon$ and converge pointwise to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$. We conducted a detailed analysis of properties of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, using (among others) the relationship between the family $\{E_{F,\varepsilon}\}_{\varepsilon\in[0,1]}$ and the family $\{E^\lambda_F(\rho)\}_{\lambda>0}$ of Moreau-Yosida approximations of the EoF explored in [arXiv:2609.30246]. We obtain a variational expression for the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ (which for $\varepsilon=0$ turns into the standard variational expression for the EoF). We also describe the weak subadditivity property of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ and analyse their continuity properties. The semicontinuity bounds for the EoF (presented in [Lob.J.Math., 46, 2632-2658],[arXiv:2404.07978]) allow us to obtain easily computable upper bounds on the rate of uniform convergence of the function $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ on the sets of states with bounded rank/energy of one of the marginal states. Applicability of the obtained results to other entanglement measures, in particular, to the relative entropy of entanglement, is discussed. As an auxiliary result, it is shown that for any state of an infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system, there exists a nearest separable state w.r.t. the trace norm distance. The non-uniqueness of such a state is also shown.

papers.title: Which Adiabatic Cycles Alter an Action Variable?
papers.abstract: Action variables are adiabatic invariants: their values are preserved during adiabatic time evolutions in completely integrable classical Hamiltonian systems. Nevertheless, an adiabatic cycle can alter how an action variable depends on phase-space variables that are independent of adiabatic parameters. Such a change, which we call action variable holonomy, induces adiabatic torus pumping in phase space. For a family of completely integrable kicked-top systems, a homotopy classification of adiabatic cycles identifies which adiabatic cycles induce action variable holonomy and adiabatic torus pumping. A physical example is also provided.

papers.title: Pareto-Optimal Hypersonic Vehicle Design with Canonical-Coordinate Neural Operator Surrogates Under Ablation-Driven Shape Change and Incidence Variation
papers.abstract: High-fidelity CFD is essential for coupled hypersonic aerodynamic and aerothermal phenomena, but its cost precludes multi-objective design optimization. We develop three DeepONet surrogates for two hypersonic configurations, unified by one device: the trunk receives coordinates in which the varying feature is held fixed. The first is a prescribed family of 37 spherically blunted tangent ogives, varied through ogive radius of curvature to span nose-tip ablation forebody change; no ablation is computed. A body-fitted canonical transformation maps every domain onto a common (s, eta) space, retaining physical coordinates for forces and heat transfer. A branch network predicts reduced coefficients and a Transolver trunk with Physics-Attention learns the spatial basis; a two-step strategy optimizes both jointly, orthonormalizes the basis by QR factorization, and trains a second-stage branch for unseen geometries. Surrogates cover density, pressure, velocity, temperatures, conductivities and species mass fractions. In leave-one-out tests, drag, mean and peak wall heat flux are recovered to 1.16%, 1.62% and 5.29%; a sweep of 1001 geometries gives a 200-design Pareto front trading 6.68% in drag for 4.42% in peak heating (a diagnostic, not an objective). The second is the 3D AEDC waverider at 29 angles of attack: static mesh, moving leading-edge shock. For surface quantities, the same construction predicts integrated heat load within 0.22% and force coefficients to errors below 2.6x10^-5; Pareto fronts identify angles of attack trading drag, lift and heating. For the volume field, a Cartesian trunk smears the shock; a frozen ShockNet supplies a shock-aligned coordinate and a hotspot-aware mixture of experts corrects the residual, recovering density to 12.28% relative L2 error at a held-out incidence (5.08x10^7 nodes). The 1001-design sweep takes about three minutes on a single CPU.

papers.title: Scaling Limits as Extensions of Continuous Bundles of C*-algebras
papers.abstract: We analyze scaling limits in algebraic quantum field theory using continuous bundles of C*-algebras. Different conditions of continuity on such bundles encode different strengths of approximation of the theory by its scaling limit. As a proof of concept, we consider the small-distance scaling limit of the theory of a massive free scalar field, which corresponds to a massless free scalar field. We provide a number of examples of local algebras of observables for which the corresponding bundle of C*-algebras representing the scaling limit is merely lower semicontinuous. Further, we construct an algebra of nonlocal observables for which the corresponding bundle of C*-algebras representing the scaling limit is uniformly continuous.

papers.title: Existence and stability of Weyl points
papers.abstract: Weyl points are quasimomentum-energy pairs in the band structure of three-dimensional periodic media at which two dispersion surfaces touch conically. They first arose in a model introduced by H. Weyl in 1929, but were first observed only recently in condensed matter physics and photonics experiments. Weyl points have been explored theoretically via numerical computation and via tight binding (discrete) models. In this article we present the first analytical treatment of Weyl points in a continuum PDE-type model. Starting with a Schr\"odinger operator whose electric potential is periodic with respect to the body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice, we introduce a small BCC-periodic magnetic vector potential that is equivariant with respect to a specific abelian group of symmetries. For magnetic Schr\"odinger operators of this type, we prove (i) that a pair of Weyl points bifurcates from a threefold degeneracy in the band structure of the underlying non-magnetic operator, and (ii) that these Weyl points are stable against small self-adjoint BCC-periodic perturbations of both the electric and magnetic vector potentials.

papers.title: Connes spectral distance as a quantum distance measure and a geometric measure of entanglement
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Connes spectral distance as a quantum distance measure and its applications in discriminating quantum states and calculating quantum entanglement. Based on finite matrix algebra, we construct a spectral triple for finite dimensional quantum states. The Connes spectral distance is a generalization to the quantum trace distance and Hilbert-Schmidt distance. The corresponding optimal elements can always be chosen to commute with the difference matrix $\Delta$, and then the optimal element and $\Delta$ can be simultaneously diagonalized. We obtain the formulas of Connes spectral distances in three different parameter regimes which depending on the spectrum of difference matrix. As applications, we show how to use spectral distances to distinguish state pairs that have the same trace distance and Hilbert-Schmidt distance. We also define a new geometric measure of entanglement based on spectral distance. These results can help us study the relationships among Connes spectral distance, quantum trace distance and other quantum distance measures. These concrete constructions are significant for studies of quantum states in the framework of noncommutative geometry.

papers.title: Stochastic dynamics generation of directed percolation using a two-channel convolutional neural network
papers.abstract: Neural networks provide a promising approach to learning and generating the stochastic dynamics of nonequilibrium systems. In this study, we propose a stochastic dynamics generative method based on a two-channel convolutional neural network, using the (1+1)-dimensional directed bond percolation model to investigate its ability to learn local stochastic transition rules and reproduce stochastic dynamics across different system sizes. The proposed method takes the current particle configuration and the control parameter as inputs, learns the conditional activation probabilities at the next time step through local convolutions, and generates stochastic temporal evolution through iterative Bernoulli sampling. The results show that the network-generated dynamics agree well with Monte Carlo simulations across different control parameters. Furthermore, applying the trained network to a substantially larger system with $L=10000$ yields an estimated critical probability of $p_c=0.643$ and an effective density decay exponent of $\delta\approx0.1592$, close to the established theoretical values. These findings demonstrate that the proposed method can reproduce the stochastic dynamics of directed percolation and capture its macroscopic dynamical and statistical properties across different spatial sizes.

papers.title: Root-of-unity limit of the $A_{n-1}$ lens elliptic gamma function solution of the star-star relation
papers.abstract: We study the root-of-unity limit of the multi-component spin solution of the star-star relation whose Boltzmann weights are products of lens elliptic gamma functions, and whose spins take values in $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\times(\mathbb{Z}_r)^{n-1}$. When one of the elliptic nomes tends to a primitive $2rN$-th root of unity, the quasi-classical expansion gives at leading order the classical star-star relation of the Bazhanov-Sergeev multi-spin model; at the next order, under the standard assumptions on the saddle points, a $(\mathbb{Z}_{rN})^{n-1}$-state solution of the star-star relation, which depends on $r$ and $N$ only through $rN$. Real $\mathbb{Z}_n$-symmetric configurations of the continuous spins give elliptic $\mathfrak{sl}(n)$ Kashiwara-Miwa type models labeled by $n$-torsion points. Extended to general primitive torsion points, these include the broken $\mathbb{Z}_{rN}$ model of Quano and Fujii, for which the star-star relation follows from their Yang-Baxter equation when $\gcd(n,rN)=1$. In the trigonometric limit the saddle point equations single out the spectral curve of the $\mathfrak{sl}(n)$ chiral Potts model of Bazhanov, Kashaev, Mangazeev and Stroganov, and the Boltzmann weights become those of that model.

papers.title: Mathematical foundations of second quantization: an introduction through spin-boson models
papers.abstract: These lecture notes originate from a one-semester course on the mathematical foundations of second quantization, first given at the Department of Physics of the Friedrich-Alexander-Universit\"at Erlangen-N\"urnberg in the Winter Semester 2025/26 to a mixed audience of physics and mathematics students. Their guiding thread is a class of physical models: spin-boson models, describing a two-level system coupled to a boson field. After summarizing the necessary background on unbounded operators, up to the Kato-Rellich and KLMN theorems, and developing direct sums and tensor products of Hilbert spaces and of unbounded operators, we treat single-mode boson fields, constructing the ladder and number operators and characterizing their domains, before moving to Fock spaces, second quantization, bosonic and fermionic annihilation and creation operators, and the canonical (anti)commutation relations. Throughout, spin-boson models provide both the motivation and the test bench for the formalism: we rigorously establish their self-adjointness, solve the pure dephasing and Jaynes-Cummings models explicitly, deriving their spectra and the qubit channels they induce, show how their multimode counterparts display irreversible decoherence and decay, and, in an appendix, prove the rotating-wave approximation for the quantum Rabi model with an explicit error bound. Finally, we use the KLMN theorem to construct spin-boson models with non-normalizable form factors, and briefly discuss stronger ultraviolet divergences and the need for renormalization. Exercises with full solutions are included.

papers.title: Area laws for free fermions in ergodic field: spectral criteria and localisation-based methods
papers.abstract: We review rigorous results concerning the Area Law for the entanglement entropy of free fermions whose one-body Hamiltonian is an ergodic Schr\"odinger operator with a strongly localised pure point spectrum. Particular attention is paid to operators with deterministic potentials (quasi-periodic ones and those generated by subshifts of finite type). Our approach relies on reducing the problem to obtaining exponential estimates for the eigenfunction correlator. This provides an effective route from localisation to the Area Law and allows for the identification of additional spectral estimates that need to be proven for various classes of ergodic operators. We realise this approach by using various localisation techniques, including dynamical localisation and the uniformly localised eigenfunction property for bounded and unbounded ergodic operators (e.g. the Maryland model), as well as a new method for obtaining the corresponding exponential bounds for Schr\"odinger operators generated by subshifts of finite type.

papers.title: A Finite-Range, Translation-Invariant Counterexample to Weak Gibbsianity
papers.abstract: We construct a finite-range, translation-invariant counterexample to the Weak Gibbsianity property for quantum spin systems on $\mathbb{Z}^2$. The proof relies on showing how a local potential can induce macroscopically large deviations from an equilibrium configuration after a perturbation is introduced at the boundary of the lattice.

papers.title: Persistence of Unitary Almost Mathieu Operator Gaps Ten Dry Martinis, Five on the Rim
papers.abstract: We determine exactly which gap labels are realized by open spectral gaps for the unitary almost Mathieu operator at every irrational frequency and all coupling constants ($0<\lambda_1,\lambda_2\leq1$). When both couplings are strictly less than one, every permitted gap label is realized by an open gap, including in the critical case ($\lambda_1=\lambda_2$). When at least one coupling equals one, both lifts of every odd winding label are realized by open gaps, whereas all even winding labels are collapsed. The proof combines quantitative almost reducibility and Aubry duality with a monotonicity principle for gap heights.

papers.title: Proof of the entropic $c$-theorem
papers.abstract: We prove an entropic $c$-theorem in two dimensions by constructing a $c$-function from the mutual information between spacelike separated wedges, defined through the relative entropy. The proof follows Casini and Huerta's, with strong subadditivity of entanglement entropy replaced by increasing differences of the mutual information, which we prove directly in the continuum from the split property and standard properties of relative entropy. The benefit of relative entropy is that every quantity we use is finite and no cutoff ever needs to be introduced. The assumptions of the theorem are only the standard axioms of algebraic quantum field theory, the split property with finite mutual information across a gap (both implied by modular $p$-nuclearity), and a finite ultraviolet bound on the resulting $c$-functions. We also note that, formally, the $c$-function is proportional to the minimal averaged null energy of a state that reproduces the vacuum correlations between the two wedges.

papers.title: Dirac Equations With All Possible Combinations of Scalar-Scalar, Vector-Vector and Pseudoscalar-Pseudoscalar Interactions
papers.abstract: We obtain exact solutions of the nonlinear Dirac (NLD) equation in $1+1$ dimensions of the form $\psi(x,t) = e^{-i\omega t} \psi(x)$ for all possible combinations of scalar-scalar (SS), vector-vector (VV) and pseudoscalar-pseudoscalar (PP) interactions at nonlinearity parameter $\kappa = 1$, which corresponds to the most general 4-Fermion interactions. We look for solutions where $0 < \omega < m$ where $\omega, m$ are frequency and mass respectively. Remarkably, we show that at $\kappa = 1$, all the NLD models with SS, VV and PP interactions can be reduced to suitable combinations of SS and VV interactions and hence all solitary waves in these models must also be bound states. We show that two of the ten possible combinations are equivalent to $SS -(1/p) VV$ interactions while two other combinations are equivalent to $VV -(1/q) SS$ interactions for which we already know the results. For the remaining six combinations of SS, VV and PP, we show that depending on the parameters, whereas in some cases entire range of $0 < \omega < m$ is allowed, in some other cases $\omega$ is restricted to a smaller range $\omega_{min} < \omega < m$. Further, depending on the parameters, while the solitary waves in some cases have only one hump, in other cases the solitary waves have both single and double hump depending on the value of $\omega$. We compute the charge $Q$ and the energy $E$ for each of the solitary wave solutions and show that while $E$ and $Q$ depend on coupling constant $g$, their ratio $E/Q$ is independent of $g$. When $\kappa = 1$, all the NLD models with SS, VV and PP interactions can be reduced to suitable combinations of SS and VV interactions. As a result all solitary waves in these models are bound states with $E/Q<m$.

papers.title: Smith Algebra from $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Tensor Product Branching via the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko Algebra
papers.abstract: Let $L_n$ be the finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module of highest weight $n$. We study the space of highest-weight vectors in $L_n\otimes L_m$ for the diagonal $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action. The extremal projector constructs these singular vectors and gives operators connecting the highest-weight lines in the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition. We interpret these operators in the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko algebra of the diagonal pair $(\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2, \mathfrak{sl}_2^{\mathrm{diag}})$. A rescaling of their quadratic relation yields the cubic Smith relation $[E,F]=2(H^3-cH)$. This cubic algebra is also known as a Higgs algebra in the physics literature. We express both the central parameter $c$ and the Smith Casimir in terms of the quadratic $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Casimir elements of the two tensor factors. The singular subspace becomes an irreducible Smith module of dimension $\min\{n,m\}+1$, with explicit formulas for the actions of the raising and lowering operators $E$ and $F$. Finally, comparison with finite-dimensional simple Smith modules gives a necessary and sufficient condition for a module to arise from this tensor-product construction.

papers.title: Longitudinal electric corner modes in continuum quantum gauge theory with matter
papers.abstract: Subregions in gauge theories give rise to edge modes and corner charges supported on their boundaries. While this is well-established classically and in quantum lattice gauge theories, the fate of corner modes remains poorly understood in continuum quantum field theories owing to their distributional nature. In this paper, we revisit this challenge and propose a new corner operator for a regional Cauchy slice algebra generated by local gauge-invariant observables of scalar QED in Minkowski spacetime. The corner mode is given by the longitudinal electric field sourced by the matter outside the subregion and thus constitutes a centre for the regional algebra. Our main goal is to show that there exists a perturbative GNS state on this algebra that quantises this mode. Pulling back the Fock vacuum to the slice, we construct this state by renormalising the divergences arising from the lack of temporal smearing. We clarify that the inclusion of the new centre mode necessitates a further renormalisation on the corner of the region, thereby physically distinguishing it and breaking the translation invariance of the state. Our work shows how the requirements of locality, renormalisability, and positivity together put strong constraints on the existence of a continuum quantum field theory which supports corner modes as genuine quantum operators. We finish with comments about the von Neumann completion of the regional algebra, as well as possible physical interpretations of the renormalised vacuum state.

papers.title: Faster-than-power-law decay of order parameter correlations in the two-dimensional RP$^2$ model: a rigorous result by vibe-proving
papers.abstract: We consider the RP$^2$ model on the two-dimensional square lattice with nearest-neighbor interactions. It is obtained by replacing the spin in the standard classical Heisenberg model with a director, which does not distinguish two opposite directions. Unlike the standard classical Heisenberg model or the O(3) nonlinear sigma model, the RP$^2$ (and its cousin RP$^3$) model allows point vortex defects classified by $\pi_1(RP^2)= Z_2$ in two dimensions. It is tempting to expect the $Z_2$ vortices to induce a phase transition analogous to the well-established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in the O(2) model (XY model) in two dimensions. Indeed, the possibilities of a critical phase or a critical point with power-law correlations of the order parameter in the RP$^2$ and RP$^3$ models have been discussed in the literature. However, the challenging nature of the problem has prevented a definitive conclusion on the phase diagram so far. In this paper, we report a rigorous mathematical proof by Artificial Intelligence (ChatGPT 6 Astra) that the absolute value of the two-point correlation function of order parameters at distance $r$ in the RP$^2$ and RP$^3$ models on the two-dimensional square lattice is bounded above by $C_\beta \exp{(-c_\beta[\log(2+r)]^2)}$ for any finite inverse temperature $\beta\ge0$, with positive constants $C_\beta$ and $c_\beta$ depending only on $\beta$. Namely, the correlation function decays faster than any power of $r$. The proof is formalized and verified in Lean; the formalization is publicly available at doi:10.5281/zenodo.23548847 . A heuristic argument based on a one-parameter effective theory ansatz at large distances combined with the rigorous correlation bound suggests (but does not prove) that the $Z_2$ vortices are always unbound at any nonzero temperature.

papers.title: Coordination three heals, coordination four is hard: the antiferromagnetic Potts model with a costly third state
papers.abstract: We study the ground states of the antiferromagnetic three-state Potts model in which the third state carries a single-ion energy cost $D_3$, on arbitrary lattices, and show that the difficulty of the ground-state problem is controlled by the maximum coordination $\Delta$ alone; on planar lattices with $\Delta\le5$ it is classified completely. On lattices with coordination at most three the third state heals frustrated bonds one for one: every graph of maximum degree three other than $K_4$ has an independent set of sites that meets every odd cycle and whose size equals the number $\operatorname{fr}$ of frustrated bonds of the Ising ground state. This identity also follows from known results on the chromatic vertex stability of graphs; we give a constructive proof. Hence $E_0 (D_3)=\min(D_3,1) \operatorname{fr}$ for all $D_3$, computable in polynomial time on planar lattices. In graph-theoretic terms, independent odd cycle transversal is solvable in polynomial time on planar subcubic graphs. On planar lattices with maximum coordination four, in contrast, deciding the ground-state energy is NP-complete for every fixed $0\le D_3<2$ and polynomial for $D_3\ge2$. The boundary is set by a local principle: a site of coordination $d$ in the third state relieves at most $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ frustrated bonds, so the third state is useless once $D_3\ge\lfloor\Delta/2\rfloor$; this threshold is sharp for every $\Delta\ge3$ and reproduces the triangular-lattice point $D_3^*=3$ of the equivalent spin-1 Blume--Capel antiferromagnet. From a single Ising ground state the proof builds an exact ground state in polynomial time, which for quasicrystalline, foam-like and defective lattices with thousands of sites takes seconds to minutes.

papers.title: Tracy Widom law for sample covariance matrices under quadratic form concentration
papers.abstract: We study sample covariance matrices formed from i.i.d., centered, isotropic random vectors $q_1, \dots, q_N \in \mathbb{R}^M$, whose coordinates are allowed to be dependent. We assume the random vectors satisfy a concentration bound for their quadratic forms $q_i^T A q_i$. Under this assumption, we establish edge universality and obtain the Tracy--Widom law for the largest eigenvalue of the sample covariance matrix after appropriate centering and scaling. In particular, our result removes the unconditionality assumption in existing edge universality results for log-concave ensembles~\cite{BX}, resolving the question that originally motivated our work. The concentration assumption also allows us to extend the result beyond the log-concave class.
